questions.text: Design an algorithm and create a flowchart to check if a given number is a palindrome.
questions.reason: Write an algorithm and draw a flowchart that reverses the digits and compares them with the original. It uses one loop, so it is Easy.

questions.text: Identify and explain the different types of computer languages, highlighting their unique characteristics and examples for each.
questions.reason: Explain machine, assembly and high-level languages with their traits and examples. It is pure theory.

questions.text:
i) Write a C program that generates a grade based on the score in a subject using a switch statement. The program should take an integer input (0 to 100) representing the student's score and should generate and display grades based on following criteria.
• 90 and above: Grade A
• 80 to 89: Grade B
• 70 to 79: Grade C
• 60 to 69: Grade D
• Below 60: Grade F
ii) Referring to the criteria in part (i) question above, write a C program to generate and display grades, using conditional (ternary) operators only [do not use if's and switch].
iii) Evaluate the following expression and provide the resultant: Consider: i = 9, j = 5.
(i * 3 + j % i + j - 1 + i - 4 / j + 1)
questions.reason: Most of the marks go to a grade program written twice, once with switch (score/10 ranges) and once with nested ternary operators. Part iii is a short operator-precedence evaluation. Every part is a single decision chain.

questions.text:
Write a C program utilizing appropriate decision-making statements to compute the commission based on the input sales amount, considering the following conditions:
a. For sales amounts less than or equal to Rs. 5000 no commission is given to females, males receive a commission of 2%.
b. For sales amounts greater than Rs. 5000 and up to Rs. 10,000 females receive a commission of 2%, males receive a commission of 4%.
c. For sales amounts exceeding Rs. 10,000, both males and females receive a commission of 6%.
questions.reason: Commission depends on both the sales slab and gender, which needs nested if/else-if. The branching is direct with no loops.

questions.text:
Write a complete C program to read a number and check for the following operations using a while Loop.
• Display "EVEN" if all the digits in the number are even.
• Display "ODD" if all the digits in the number are odd.
• Display "neither EVEN nor ODD" if all the digits in the number are neither even nor odd.
questions.reason: Take digits off with % and / in a while loop and track whether they are all even or all odd. It needs one loop and two flags.

questions.text: Explain the significance of a 1D array in programming and its practical applications. Discuss various methods for initializing an array. Additionally, write a C program that reads N elements into a single array and then separates the elements into two arrays: one containing prime numbers and the other containing non-prime numbers.
questions.reason: Explain 1D arrays and how to initialize them, then split an array into prime and non-prime arrays. Each element needs a nested primality loop, which is still standard first-year work.

questions.text: Write a C program to count the number of alphabets, digits, and special characters in a given string.
questions.reason: Scan the string once and sort each character into alphabet, digit or special. It is a single loop with range checks.

questions.text: Write a C program to read the elements of a 3 × 3 matrix and sort the elements of each row in ascending order. Display the matrix after sorting each row.
questions.reason: Read a 3x3 matrix and bubble-sort each row separately. The nested loops over a fixed small matrix are routine.

questions.text:
Design and implement a menu-driven C program using functions (without using structures) to manage student records. The program should allow the user to:
1. Add new student details (Name, Roll Number, Marks)
2. Display all student details
3. Search for a student by roll number
4. Calculate and display the class average marks
questions.reason: Build a menu-driven record manager from functions that add, display, search by roll number and average the marks, without structures. Keeping parallel arrays in step across functions makes it Medium.

questions.text:
Write a C program using functions to calculate Simple Interest (SI), Compound Interest (CI), and their Difference. The program should take the principal, rate, and time as inputs and use separate functions for each calculation - one for SI, one for CI, and one for finding the difference. Demonstrate how using multiple functions improves the program's modularity, readability, and reusability.
Hint: SI = (P × R × T) / 100, CI = P ((1 + R / 100)^T) – P
questions.reason: Write separate functions for SI, CI and their difference using the given formulas, then comment on modularity. It is direct formula evaluation.

questions.text: Design a program using functions with pointer parameters to compute both row-wise and column-wise sums of a matrix.
questions.reason: Pass the matrix through pointer parameters and compute row and column sums. The point being tested is pointer access to a 2D array, and the sums are plain nested loops.

questions.text: Write a C program using separate functions to perform operations on an array. Implement readArray() to input n integers, reverseArray() to reverse the array elements, findMaximum() to find the maximum value in the reversed array, and displayResult() to print both the reversed array and the maximum element. Each function should handle its task independently, and data should be passed appropriately between functions.
questions.reason: Split read, reverse, find-maximum and display into separate functions that share the array. Each function is one simple loop.

questions.text:
A shop maintains information about its products, including product_name, quantity, and price. You are required to use an array of structures and pointer arithmetic in C to perform the following task and display the details (product_name, quantity, and price) of products whose quantity is less than 5.:
i) Calculate the total stock value of all products (where stock value of each product = quantity × price).
questions.reason: Loop over an array of product structures with pointer arithmetic, print the low-stock items and sum quantity × price. It is one pass with a filter.

questions.text: Analyze the difference in accessing structure members using a normal structure variable and a pointer to structure. Write a C program showing both methods.
questions.reason: Contrast the dot operator with the arrow operator for structure access and show both in a short program. It is a concept demonstration.

questions.text: Develop a C program to merge two text files (file1.txt and file2.txt) into a third file (merged.txt). After merging, the program should display the total number of characters and lines in the merged file. Explain how file pointers and end-of-file (EOF) checks contribute to efficient file concatenation.
questions.reason: Merge two text files into a third with EOF-controlled loops, then count the characters and lines in the result and explain file pointers. The rubric rates file merging with checks as Medium.
